choices.text: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem, so producers get it back again
Energy cycles between producers and decomposers only
Energy flows one way through the ecosystem and leaves as heat
Energy is destroyed at the top of the food chain

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. The "cycle of life" language makes energy sound like it loops round forever. Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water, as scene s6 shows.
questions.misconception: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.
questions.prompt: A student says energy keeps cycling round an ecosystem forever, coming back to the producers. What is correct?

choices.text: From feeder to food, predator to prey
From food to feeder, in the direction of energy flow
From the largest animal to the smallest
In a circle, back to the producers

questions.explanation: Scene s1 gives the rule: arrows follow energy flow, pointing from food to feeder - grass to rabbit to fox.
questions.prompt: Which direction do arrows point in a food chain?

questions.answer: Most energy is lost as heat from respiration, in egestion and excretion, and in uneaten or undigested parts, so only about a tenth is built into new tissue that the next level can eat.
questions.explanation: Scene s3 shows the dot shrinking as it climbs the pyramid: each level keeps only a tenth of the energy, so the pyramid narrows fast.
questions.prompt: Explain why only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next level, and what happens to the rest.

questions.answer: Energy flows one way: sunlight in, heat out. Carbon cycles: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, while respiration, combustion and decomposition return CO2 to the air.
questions.explanation: Scenes s4 and s6 separate the two: the carbon dot loops round and round, while the energy dot enters as sunlight and leaves as heat, never returning.
questions.prompt: Compare how energy and carbon move through an ecosystem: state which one cycles and which flows one way, naming the processes involved.

choices.text: The species moved because energy is recycled elsewhere
Habitat loss and fragmentation left fragments too small and isolated to support the species
The pyramid of energy inverted in the fragments
Decomposers stopped cycling carbon in the fragments

questions.explanation: Scene s5 shows each patch shrinking under pressure and its species label vanishing with it: lose the habitat and the species that need it vanish too.
questions.prompt: A forest is cleared into small isolated fragments and a wide-ranging species disappears. What is the best explanation?
